text: Highly recommended! I had a great hypnotherapy session with Nick after a friend recommended his wellness center. Nick understood my feelings and I felt relieved afterward. The booking process is easy. You can book an appointment online and have an intro call first. The center has a relaxing atmosphere, good for therapy. The location is excellent. It's not that far from the city with its own car park. Great service all around!

My partner and I have had multiple sessions with Nick and we've both seen significant improvements in our relationship, even from the very first session.

I strongly believe that any couples going through relationship struggles, misunderstandings and constantly triggering each other would greatly benefit from having sessions with Nick.

Nick is masterfully intuitive in his craft and is able to quickly pinpoint areas that will really move the needle towards healing and growth. After just  a single session, triggers that would often cause a reaction would no longer happen, and over the course of several sessions, Nick helped us to untangle a web of deep rooted traumas that we each had, to help us heal and move towards healthier expressions towards one another.

I had an incredible experience with Nicholas. He was able to understand my problem right away and identify the blockage I wasn’t even fully aware of. With just one session, he guided me through hypnosis in such a kind, smart, and professional way that the issue completely transformed—I don’t struggle with it anymore.

He is very experienced, attentive, and makes you feel comfortable immediately. I’m truly impressed by his ability to get straight to the root of the problem and help me release it so effectively. I highly recommend him to anyone looking for real and lasting change.

I saw Nick while I was in Chiang Mai after several weeks at The Dawn, which is a residential treatment centre where people go to stabilise and work through trauma, addiction, and other mental health struggles. During my time there I had been doing fairly intensive therapy, including a series of EMDR sessions, which stands for Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing, a trauma therapy designed to help the brain process difficult memories. Part of why I booked with him was a genuine hope that, after doing that work, I might finally be more open or responsive to another modality. He kindly fitted me in at short notice with an early morning appointment, and I actually adjusted my plans and left The Dawn a day earlier than intended in order to make it work. Even then, it was still a significant journey from where I was staying, so I did not come to the session casually. I came wanting it to matter. Nick himself was professional, punctual, and courteous throughout. We spent the opening part of the session going over my background, which made sense given the complexity of what I had sent him beforehand and the fact that he was about to leave town. Still, by the time we moved into the hypnotherapy itself, I was left with the feeling that the part I had really come for was more limited than I expected. What stayed with me most was not offence or discomfort, but disappointment. I had hoped I might finally be receptive to this kind of work, especially after the trauma processing I had already begun. Instead, I found myself in that familiar position of being unable to absorb very much from it. The experience felt largely like being guided verbally through imagery and suggestions. I understand that this is essentially how hypnotherapy works in practice, but for someone with a very analytical and hyper-vigilant mind it can feel almost indistinguishable from simply listening to someone speak or guide a meditation. In my case, I struggled to enter the state that the method depends on, so the technique itself didn’t really land for me. I also didn’t feel much of a therapeutic spark or warmth in the room, which matters to me more than technical professionalism alone. He was perfectly proper, but I didn’t leave with the sense of having encountered anything particularly memorable, intuitive, or unusually attuned. At 6,000 baht for 90 minutes, that made the experience hard to justify on a value level, at least for me. To be fair, he did follow up afterwards with a thoughtful message reflecting on our conversation, which I appreciated. I also want to mention Anna, his wife, who was the one who first responded when I called the clinic. She struck me as genuinely warm and welcoming on the phone, and when I briefly met her in person she left a very kind impression. Her warmth stood out. So this is not a hostile review, nor is it an attempt to undermine the many people who clearly have had meaningful experiences with him. It is simply my own honest account. For me, the modality didn’t land, the connection didn’t quite form, and the cost made that harder to overlook.

In case you are wary of the term “hypnotherapy”, I will break down my experience. The first 30 minutes were more like traditional talk therapy, then Nick guided me through some breathwork and relaxation exercises to get me in a relaxed and receptive state. Then he guides you through a series of what I can best described as guided meditations and visualizations, he asks some questions, and I was welcome to speak at any time, but for the majority of the hypnosis portion of the session, Nick was doing the talking / guiding.
I don’t know much about reiki, but I know that Nick is a reiki master and I now know that I would never want to do hypnotherapy with someone who is not a reiki master. His ability to follow the energy and manipulate the energy was one of the craziest things I have ever experienced in my life.
My primary goal in these sessions was nervous system regulation. I am 2 weeks out from my time with Nick, and in those two weeks my HRV has increased by about 40% on average. (HRV is the key biometric indicator of if your nervous system is in fight/flight or rest/relax. The higher the number, the better). And I have felt a noticeable lightness and expansion in my body and mind. It may be too soon to tell, but my intuition says this feels permanent.
My primary feedback to Nick was “I did not expect that to be so entertaining.” In the hypnotic state, I felt like I had my consciousness there watching the whole process unfold. And the theatrics that my subconscious and nervous system had to share were wildly entertaining to me. My sessions were immensely healing and helpful, but I can also describe them to others with lightness and laughter.
In my experience, I was quite surprised that the things that came up in my session were not these moments of ultimate trauma and darkness, but rather misunderstandings of things that happened when I was a child, that are now very easy to understand and process as an adult. I don’t assume that will be everyone’s experience, but perhaps it is a reasonable expectation that the wounds that set you up for some darkness later in life are more easily addressed and healed than you might think, with the right guide and container.
